drivingQuestion: Does the mishna's 'on all, if he recited SheHakol he fulfilled' include bread and wine, which have their own blessings?
outcomeNote: The amoraic dispute is stated without resolution in this unit; the discussion continues in the following unit

segments.he: וְעַל כּוּלָּן אִם אָמַר ״שֶׁהַכֹּל״ וְכוּ׳. אִתְּמַר. רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: חוּץ מִן הַפַּת וּמִן הַיַּיִן. וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ פַּת וְיַיִן.
segments.en: We learned in the mishna: «And on all» food items, «if he recited:» By whose word «all things» came to be, he fulfilled his obligation. «It was stated» that the amora’im disputed the precise explanation of the mishna. «Rav Huna said:» This halakha applies to all foods «except for bread and wine.» Since they have special blessings, one does not fulfill his obligation by reciting the general blessing: By whose word all things came to be. «And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» One fulfills his obligation with the blessing: By whose word all things came to be, «even» over «bread and wine.»

moves.cueHe: אתמר. רב הונא אמר: חוץ מן הפת ומן היין
moves.summary: Reads the mishna's 'on all' as excluding bread and wine
moves.about: carves bread and wine out of the mishna's 'on all', since they have their own blessings

moves.cueHe: ורבי יוחנן אמר: אפילו פת ויין
moves.summary: Reads the mishna's 'on all' as including even bread and wine
moves.about: reads the mishna's 'on all' as including even bread and wine
